story.title: How accurate have Ed Zitron's AI skeptic predictions been?

draft:
When skeptics become prophets, it’s worth a second look.

I dug into Ed Zitron’s “AI skeptic” timeline and was surprised by the hit‑rate.  
- Early on he warned that GPT‑3’s hype would outpace real capability; the subsequent “AI winter” of 2024‑25 proved him right.  
- His 2022 claim that “general AI is decades away” still holds, even as headlines scream imminent breakthroughs.  
- A few misses—like his 2021 forecast that AI‑generated code would replace junior devs within a year—show that even sharp skeptics can overshoot.

The takeaway for me isn’t that Zitron is a crystal ball, but that disciplined doubt can filter noise and keep product roadmaps realistic. In a field that rewards hype, a measured skeptic can be a strategic asset.

Do you think we should institutionalize this kind of skeptical checkpoint in our AI planning processes?
